condition: severe needle anxiety at 14 weeks gestation causing avoidance of every routine prenatal blood draw
level_rationale: At 14 weeks of pregnancy, severe needle fear that repeatedly causes the patient to leave the laboratory before every routine prenatal blood draw prevents essential obstetric infectious, hematologic, and Rh screening and warrants structured exposure therapy and applied-tension training with a therapist, whereas feeling brief mild nervousness and looking away calmly during a routine pregnancy blood draw is normal transient venipuncture uneasiness requiring no clinical intervention beyond self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (14 weeks pregnant, routine prenatal blood draws, and intense needle fear causing departure from the lab before every draw) without naming trypanophobia, with a 1-word span difference (16 vs 17 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets ({14}) across all 6 variants.
